newsitem.title: USA: Dow index extends last week's runup.
newsitem.headline: Dow index extends last week's runup.

text.p: Blue chips rose Monday, following through on last week's strength that sparked the Dow Jones industrial average to three straight sessions of record highs, but the rally was restrained by caution ahead of key of economic data.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow was up 31.31 points to 6,251.13, beating Friday's record finish of 6,219.82.
Last week's gain of 198 points was the second-biggest weekly rise since the 206.77-point surge in the week of Aug. 2 this year.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 11-9 on subdued volume of 193 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 1.34 points at 1,258.85, while the American Stock Exchange index was off 2.25 at 578.14.
The bond market was closed for the Veterans' Day holiday.
"There are a lot of important numbers due out this week and the market will look to them for inspiration," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

Data include October producer and consumer price indices on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively. The October retail sales report is due Thursday, and the October industrial production and capacity utilization report is due on Friday.
Another key event will be Wednesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee, which will weigh monetary policy against the background of recent economic reports.

"This is a pretty important week. We have the Fed meeting coming and two of the most important numbers about inflation, the CPI and PPI," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"I think we are going to be stronger in the second half of the fourth quarter on the demand side, meaning consumer credit and spending," he said.
Bleier said the Fed will be closely watching the pricing components of the CPI and PPI.
"So long as the economy is growing but pricing is stable, they won't do anything," he said.

"There are some people talking about the Fed making an easing move," Bleier said. "They are totally deluding themselves. Britain just raised rates a week ago and there is talk of Japan raising rates. If all the other industrialised countries are raising rates, guess what?"
Technology stocks were mixed, with Intel Corp. down 5/8 at 121-5/8 and Microsoft Corp. up 3/8 at 143-7/8. Hewlett-Packard Co. was up one at 48-3/8.
Johnson said the Dow had an upside potential of about 9 percent, or to 6,800 from its current level, over the next 12 months unless the market grew speculative or euphoric.

Among special situations, IVAX Corp. and Bergen Brunswig sold off after the companies agreed to merge. IVAX was down 2-7/8 at 12-7/8 while Bergen Brunswig fell four to 28-3/4 as some traders said the $1.65 billion stock-swap deal valued IVAX shares below market value as of Friday's close.
PHH Corp. surged 17-1/4 to 48 on news that it agreed to be taken over by HFS Inc. in a $1.7 billion stock-swap deal. HFS was off 3/8 at 73-3/4.
